definition_en: a stick of wax with a string through the middle that is burned to give light
core_image: 一支点燃的蜡烛，火苗在黑暗里轻轻摇晃
scene: 停电的那个晚上，妹妹点燃了一支蜡烛，小小的火光把房间照亮。When the lights went out, my little sister lit a candle in the dark room.
sceneCN: 这里 candle 是「蜡烛」（第 1 个义项：用蜡做成、点燃照明的细长物）；句意为停电的晚上，妹妹点燃蜡烛照亮房间。

collocations.phrase: burn the candle at both ends
collocations.zh: 过度消耗精力；两头燃烧

derivatives.zh: 由 candle 加 light 构成，义为「烛光」
历史上指做蜡烛或卖蜡烛的商人，今多指船具商

senses.title: A wax stick that burns for light
senses.definition: a cylinder of wax with a wick inside that gives light when burned
senses.definitionCN: 中间有烛芯、点燃后发光的蜡制圆柱
senses.example: Grandma put a candle on my birthday cake.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶在我生日蛋糕上放了一支蜡烛。
senses.why: Fire in a wax stick is a simple, ancient way to make light, so the object is named directly by what it does.
senses.whyCN: 一根蜡里装上火芯就能发光，这是最古老简单的照明方式，词便按用途直接命名。

senses.title: Anything shaped like a candle
senses.definition: an object shaped like a candle, such as a wax roll or a column of rock
senses.definitionCN: 形状像蜡烛的东西，如蜡卷或钟乳石柱
senses.example: Stalactites hang from the cave roof like giant candles.
senses.exampleCN: 钟乳石从洞顶垂下，像巨大的蜡烛。
senses.why: Things that share the shape of a candle borrow its name by likeness.
senses.whyCN: 凡外形与蜡烛相似的物体，都可借它的名字来称呼。

intro.en: Candle comes from a Latin word for something white and shining, carried into English through Old English.
intro.cn: candle 来自拉丁语中指「白色发亮之物」的词，经古英语进入英文。

items.en: Latin candela meant a light or torch, built on candere, to shine white.
items.cn: 拉丁语 candela 指灯或火把，词根 candere 意为发白光。

items.en: Old English took the word as candel for a wax light.
items.cn: 古英语借入为 candel，指蜡制灯火。

items.en: In Middle English the spelling settled as candle and the church candle became common.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写定型为 candle，教堂用烛十分普遍。

items.en: German Kerze shows the same borrowed root in another Germanic tongue.
items.cn: 德语 Kerze 显示同一拉丁词根在另一日耳曼语中的影子。

items.en: Today candle names real wax lights and anything shaped like them.
items.cn: 今天 candle 既指真正的蜡烛，也指一切烛状物。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects other light sources.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收其他光源类词。

entries.definition: The part of a door or tool that you hold.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「把手」，拼写与 candle 接近。
名词，义为「沙子」，读音与 candle 词首接近。
动词，义为「点燃；激起」，拼写与 candle 相近。

entries.definition: A device that uses oil or electricity to give light.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灯」，与蜡烛同为照明物。

entries.definition: A stick that burns at one end to light the way.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「火把」，是更古老的照明工具。

entries.definition: A case that protects a light from wind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灯笼」，用来护住火光。

normalIntro.en: Remember candle by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 candle。

normal.en: cand- means shine white, so a candle is a little shining stick.
normal.cn: 词根 cand- 表示「发白光」，candle 就是发光的小棒。

normal.en: candlelight is the light a candle makes.
normal.cn: candlelight 即烛光，两个词直接拼合。

normal.en: blow out the candle on your birthday cake is a fixed scene.
normal.cn: 生日蛋糕上吹蜡烛是固定场景。

normal.en: chandler was once the candle seller.
normal.cn: chandler 旧时指卖蜡烛的商人。

normal.en: kindle and candle share the feeling of starting a flame.
normal.cn: kindle 与 candle 都与点火的感觉相关。

abstract.en: Picture one small flame pushing back the whole dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象一小簇火苗顶开整个黑暗的房间。

abstract.en: Hear the wick crackle softly in the quiet night.
abstract.cn: 静夜里仿佛听见烛芯轻轻的噼啪声。

abstract.en: Feel the warm wax slowly dripping down the side.
abstract.cn: 感受温热的蜡油沿烛身缓缓滑落。

examples.en: The room was dark, so she lit a candle.
examples.cn: 房间很暗，于是她点了一支蜡烛。

examples.en: He blew out the candles and made a wish.
examples.cn: 他吹灭蜡烛许了一个愿。

examples.en: Stalactites in the cave look like giant candles.
examples.cn: 洞里的钟乳石看起来像巨大的蜡烛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坎得儿」——坎上点得儿一支蜡烛，照亮小屋。

root: 拉丁语 candere（发白光）→ candela（灯火）→ 古英语 candel → 现代英语 candle；同根词有 candid（坦白的）、incandescent（白热的）。

sensesIntro.en: Candle moves from the wax light itself to anything shaped like it.
sensesIntro.cn: candle 由真实的蜡烛扩展到一切形似蜡烛之物。

core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中挺立的一小簇火光

intro.en: Candle shows the Latin shining root cand- inside an everyday object.
intro.cn: candle 的词身藏着拉丁语「发光」词根 cand-。

latinIntro.en: The root candere, to glow white, lives on in several English words.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 candere（发白光）保留在多个英语词中。

items.meaning: honest and open, shining white in old use
items.meaningCN: 坦白的（旧义为洁白明亮）

items.example: An incandescent bulb lit the hall.

items.meaning: old word for a candle maker
items.example: The chandler sold wax by the pound.
Silver candelabra stood on the table.

definition_en: a sweet food made with sugar or chocolate, often eaten as a small treat
core_image: 五颜六色的糖纸包着小小的甜块
scene: 超市的货架上，一排彩色包装的糖果正等着被挑选。On the shop shelf a row of brightly wrapped candy waited to be picked.
sceneCN: 这里 candy 是「糖果」（第 1 个义项：用糖或巧克力做的甜食）；句意为货架上一排彩包糖果等着被挑走。

derivatives.zh: 由 candy 加 -ed 构成，义为「裹了糖衣的；蜜饯的」
由 candy 加 floss 构成，英式说法，义为「棉花糖」

senses.title: A small sweet made of sugar
senses.definition: a small piece of sweet food made with sugar or chocolate
senses.definitionCN: 用糖或巧克力做的小块甜食
senses.example: She bought a bag of candy after school.
senses.exampleCN: 放学后她买了一袋糖果。
senses.why: The Arabic word for sugar entered European languages, and the treat made from it simply took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语的「糖」一词进入欧洲语言，用糖做的小零食便直接沿用其名。

senses.title: Cooking coated or preserved in sugar
senses.definition: food cooked and preserved in sugar or syrup
senses.definitionCN: 用糖或糖浆裹住保存的食物
senses.example: The candied fruit sits on top of the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 糖渍水果摆在蛋糕顶上。
senses.why: Sugar both sweetens and preserves, so the word also names the sugar-coating process.
senses.whyCN: 糖既增甜又防腐，于是这个词也指裹糖这道工序。

intro.en: Candy traces back through French to an Arabic word for sugar itself.
intro.cn: candy 经法语上溯至阿拉伯语中表示「糖」本身的词。

items.en: Latin canna carried the cane plant name from Greek, the raw material of sugar.
items.cn: 拉丁语 canna 承载了来自希腊语的甘蔗之名，即制糖原料。

items.en: The sugar craft passed through Sanskrit khanda, a piece of sugar, into Arabic qand.
items.cn: 制糖术经梵语 khanda（糖块）传入阿拉伯语 qand。

items.en: Old French sucre candi meant sugar candy, crystallised sugar.
items.cn: 古法语 sucre candi 指结晶的冰糖。

items.en: English borrowed the word as candi around the thirteenth century for crystallised sugar.
items.cn: 十三世纪前后英语借入 candi，指冰糖。

items.en: American English shortened it to candy for all sweets, while British English keeps sweets.
items.cn: 美式英语将其简化为 candy 泛指糖果，英式英语则多用 sweets。

note.en: The first group collects look-alike words; the second collects other sugary treats.
note.cn: 第一组收形近词，第二组收其他甜食类词。

entries.definition: A wax stick that burns for light.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜡烛」，拼写与 candy 相近。

entries.definition: A cover hung or held above something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「顶篷」，词首与 candy 接近。

entries.definition: The hollow stem of the sugar plant, or a walking stick.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「甘蔗茎；手杖」，与 candy 同根。

entries.definition: British English for a piece of candy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式英语的「糖果」。
名词，义为「巧克力」，甜食的一种。
名词，义为「太妃糖」，硬质糖的一种。

normalIntro.en: Remember candy through its sugar root.
normalIntro.cn: 借糖词根记忆 candy。

normal.en: cand- comes through Arabic qand, the word for sugar.
normal.cn: 词根经阿拉伯语 qand 而来，本义就是糖。

normal.en: candy and cane share the sugar-plant story.
normal.cn: candy 与 cane 都来自甘蔗的故事。

normal.en: cotton candy is light as a cloud.
normal.cn: cotton candy 棉花糖轻如云朵。

normal.en: candied fruit keeps for months in sugar.
normal.cn: 糖渍水果靠糖保存数月。

normal.en: a candy store is full of colours.
normal.cn: 糖果店里色彩缤纷。

abstract.en: Feel the hard shell crack and the sweet centre melt.
abstract.cn: 想象糖壳碎裂、甜心融化的瞬间。

abstract.en: Hear the crinkle of a candy wrapper in a quiet class.
abstract.cn: 安静教室里糖纸的窸窣声。

abstract.en: Picture a jar of bright candies like small jewels.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐糖果像小宝石般闪亮。

examples.en: He gave each guest a piece of candy.
examples.cn: 他给每位客人一颗糖果。

examples.en: The cake is covered with candied fruit.
examples.cn: 蛋糕上铺满了糖渍水果。

examples.en: My little brother hides candy in his pocket.
examples.cn: 我弟弟把糖果藏在口袋里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看地」——看到地上一颗糖，赶紧捡起来吃。

root: 梵语 khanda（糖块）→ 阿拉伯语 qand → 古法语 sucre candi（冰糖）→ 英语 candy；同根词 cane（甘蔗茎）、candied（糖渍的）。

sensesIntro.en: Candy moves from plain sugar crystals to all small sweets and to sugar-coated food.
sensesIntro.cn: candle 由冰糖结晶扩展到一切小甜食及糖渍食物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bright block of sugar
core.cn: 核心意象：一小块亮晶晶的糖

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 canna 指甘蔗，其汁液即糖的来源。

items.example: She shares her candy with friends.

items.example: Candied ginger is spicy and sweet.
The syrup turns candy when cooled.
Workers cut sugar cane by hand.

items.exampleCN: 糖精是一种人造甜味剂。

definition_en: a soft hat without a brim behind, a close-fitting cover for a container, or a fixed upper limit
core_image: 一顶棒球帽扣在头上，也像瓶盖扣住瓶口
scene: 运动会上，教练给每个队员发了一顶红色的棒球帽。At the sports meet the coach gave every player a red cap.
sceneCN: 这里 cap 是「帽子」（第 1 个义项：无后檐的软帽）；句意为运动会教练给队员发红帽子。

collocations.zh: 毕恭毕敬地；低声下气地

senses.title: A soft head covering
senses.definition: a soft hat that fits closely, often with a front brim
senses.definitionCN: 紧贴头部的软帽，常带前檐
senses.example: He wears a blue cap on sunny days.
senses.exampleCN: 晴天他总戴一顶蓝帽子。
senses.why: A small cover for the head is the plainest image behind cap.
senses.whyCN: 罩在头顶的小小护盖，正是 cap 最朴素的画面。

senses.title: A cover for a bottle or tube
senses.definition: a small cover that closes a bottle, pen or tube
senses.definitionCN: 盖住瓶、笔或管子的小盖
senses.example: Twist the cap off the toothpaste.
senses.exampleCN: 把牙膏盖拧开。
senses.why: Anything that sits on top like a hat is also a cap, so bottles wear caps too.
senses.whyCN: 凡像帽子一样扣在顶上的东西都是 cap，瓶子也「戴帽」。

senses.title: An upper limit
senses.definition: a fixed limit that something cannot go above
senses.definitionCN: 不许突破的固定限度
senses.example: The city set a cap on taxi numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市给出租车数量设了上限。
senses.why: A cover stops things from rising out, so a limit becomes a cap too.
senses.whyCN: 盖子挡住里面的东西冒出来，限度便也成了「盖」。

intro.en: Cap comes from Latin caput, the head, through Old French chapeau-like forms.
intro.cn: cap 源自拉丁语 caput（头），经古法语相关形式进入英语。

items.en: Latin caput meant head, the source of a whole word family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caput 意为「头」，是整个词族的源头。

items.en: Late Latin cappa meant a hood or head cover.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cappa 指风帽或头罩。

items.en: Old French chape and chapel carried the hood sense into French.
items.cn: 古法语 chape 与 chapel 保留风帽之义。

items.en: English took cap in the late Old English period for a head covering.
items.cn: 古英语晚期英语借入 cap，指头部护盖。

items.en: Today cap names hats, lids and even spending limits.
items.cn: 今天 cap 兼指帽子、瓶盖乃至支出上限。

note.en: The first group collects shape and sound twins; the second collects head-and-cover relatives.
note.cn: 第一组收形音近词，第二组收「头与覆盖」的同族词。

entries.definition: A small open container for drinks.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杯子」，读音与 cap 接近。

entries.definition: A device that controls the flow of water.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「水龙头」，拼写与 cap 相近。

entries.definition: A sleeveless coat, or a piece of land jutting into the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「披肩；海角」，与 cap 同根。

entries.definition: Headwear, often with a brim all round.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「帽子」，泛指各类头饰。

entries.definition: A cover for a pot or box.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「盖子」，指锅盒之盖。

normal.en: a bottle wears a cap like a little hat.

normal.en: capital letters are the big heads of the alphabet.

normal.en: a salary cap puts a roof over pay.
normal.cn: 工资上限给薪水封了顶。

abstract.en: Picture the cap snapping on like a helmet.
abstract.cn: 想象瓶盖像头盔一样咔哒扣上。

abstract.en: Feel the brim shading your eyes from the sun.
abstract.cn: 感受帽檐替你挡住阳光。

abstract.en: See the number stop at an invisible ceiling.
abstract.cn: 想象数字撞上一道无形的天花板。

examples.en: She pushed the cap back on the pen.
examples.cn: 她把笔帽扣回去了。

examples.en: The team wore matching red caps.
examples.cn: 队员们戴着统一的红帽子。

examples.en: The rules put a cap on class size.

intro.en: The Latin head root cap- powers a wide family of English words.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「头」词根 cap- 撑起庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: From caput, the head, English gained words for leaders, tops and headings.
latinIntro.cn: 从 caput（头）衍生出英语中表首领、顶端与标题的词。

items.example: Caput is the source of cap.
items.exampleCN: caput 是 cap 的源头。

items.example: A cap covers the top of your head.

items.meaning: one who heads a team or ship

definition_zh: 首都；资本；大写字母；首要的
definition_en: the city where a government sits, money used in business, an uppercase letter, or something chief and most important
core_image: 一座城市的中心矗立着政府大楼，一切从「头」开始
scene: 地理课上，老师指着地图让学生找出各国的首都。In geography class the teacher asked us to point at each capital on the map.
sceneCN: 这里 capital 是「首都」（第 1 个义项：政府所在的城市）；句意为地理课上找各国首都。

derivatives.zh: 由 capital 加 -ism 构成，义为「资本主义」
由 capital 加 -ize 构成，义为「把…大写；利用」
同根词，义为「队长；船长」

senses.title: The head city of a country
senses.definition: the city where the government of a country or region sits
senses.definitionCN: 一国或一地区政府所在的城市
senses.example: Paris is the capital of France.
senses.exampleCN: 巴黎是法国的首都。
senses.why: The head city is the head of the country, so caput names it directly.
senses.whyCN: 一国之首即「头城」，caput 直接命名了它。

senses.title: Money used to make more money
senses.definition: money or assets used to start or grow a business
senses.definitionCN: 用于创办或扩大生意的资金
senses.example: They raised capital for the new factory.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为建新厂筹集了资本。
senses.why: Wealth is the head of an enterprise, the source from which everything grows.
senses.whyCN: 财富是企业的「头」，一切由此生长。

senses.title: Uppercase letters
senses.definition: letters written in their large form, used at the start of names and sentences
senses.definitionCN: 字母的大写形式，用于句首与专名
senses.example: Write your name in capital letters.
senses.exampleCN: 用大写字母写你的名字。
senses.why: The big letter is the head letter of the alphabet's shape family.
senses.whyCN: 大写字母是字母「形族」中的大头。

senses.title: Chief and first in importance
senses.definition: first in importance, or excellent in informal British use
senses.definitionCN: 最重要的，或英式口语中的「极好」
senses.example: Safety is a capital concern in the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 安全是实验室的首要问题。
senses.why: What stands at the head of the list is what matters most.
senses.whyCN: 排在最前、居于首位的东西最为要紧。

intro.en: Capital grows entirely from Latin caput, the head, branching into cities, money and letters.
intro.cn: capital 完全由拉丁语 caput（头）生长出城市、金钱与字母诸义。

items.en: Caput meant head, and also the head or top of anything.
items.cn: caput 意为头，也指事物的顶端。

items.en: Capitalis meant of the head, hence chief or principal.
items.cn: 形容词 capitalis 意为「属于头的」，引申为首要的。

items.en: Old French passed capitalis on as capital with the same chief sense.
items.cn: 古法语将 capitalis 传为 capital，保留首要之义。

senses.title: A road vehicle for passengers
senses.definition: a vehicle with an engine and four wheels for carrying a few people

senses.example: Our car broke down on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 我们家的车在回家路上抛锚了。

senses.title: A section of a train

intro.en: Car descends from Latin carrus, a two-wheeled wagon, through Norman French.
intro.cn: car 经诺曼法语上溯至拉丁语 carrus（双轮车）。

items.en: Latin carrus meant a Gallic two-wheeled wagon.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carrus 指高卢人的双轮车。

items.en: Norman French carre or car brought the wagon word to England.
items.cn: 诺曼法语 carre 把「车」一词带到英格兰。

items.en: Middle English car meant any wheeled cart or carriage.
items.cn: 中古英语 car 泛指各类轮车。

items.en: Related Old English cræt gave cart, a sibling word.
items.cn: 相关的古英语 cræt 衍生出 cart 一词，与 car 是兄弟词。

items.en: Nineteenth-century rail use named coaches, and the engine car took the word for good.
items.cn: 十九世纪先指车厢，随后汽车普及，car 一词专指汽车。

note.en: The first group collects wheel-word siblings; the second collects vehicle words.

entries.definition: A vehicle with two or four wheels pulled by hand or animal.

senses.title: A stiff paper for writing or greeting

senses.title: Playing cards
senses.definition: small stiff cards with numbers and pictures used in games

definition_en: to feel concern and interest, or the attention and work given to protect someone or something
core_image: 双手捧着易碎的东西，轻轻护住
scene: 下雨了，同桌把伞往我这边挪了挪。My deskmate shifted her umbrella towards me to show how much she cared.
sceneCN: 这里 care 是「关心；在意」（第 1 个义项：心里挂念对方）；句意为同桌挪伞给我，以示关心。

derivatives.zh: 由 care 加 -ful 构成，义为「小心的；仔细的」

senses.title: To feel concern for someone
senses.definition: to feel that someone or something matters to you
senses.definitionCN: 觉得某人某物对你是要紧的
senses.example: She really cares about her friends.
senses.exampleCN: 她真心关心朋友们。
senses.why: Old English caru meant a heavy mind full of worry, and worry grows where something matters.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 caru 指满怀忧虑的心，而忧虑正是因对方要紧而生。

senses.title: To look after someone or something
senses.definition: to do what is needed to keep someone healthy, safe and well
senses.definitionCN: 做让某人健康安全所需之事
senses.example: The nurse cares for the patients every day.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每天照料病人。
senses.why: When a matter sits heavy in the mind, the hands follow with daily tending.
senses.whyCN: 心里挂着的事，手上便有了日常的照料。

senses.title: Attention to avoid mistakes
senses.definition: attention and effort to avoid harm or error
senses.definitionCN: 避免伤害或出错的用心
senses.example: Handle the glass with care.
senses.exampleCN: 拿玻璃杯要小心。
senses.why: A worried mind moves slowly and checks twice, which is exactly carefulness.
senses.whyCN: 挂心的心走得很慢、再三核对，这正是「小心」。

intro.en: Care began as an old word for a heavy, worried mind.

items.en: Modern English stressed warm concern, daily tending and carefulness.

definition_zh: 携带；搬运；运送；支撑；传染（疾病）
definition_en: to hold something and take it from one place to another, or to support and transmit
core_image: 双手抱着行李，一步一步把重量挪过站台

senses.title: To hold and move something
senses.definition: to hold a person or thing and take it to another place
senses.definitionCN: 抱、扛、提着人或物移往别处
senses.example: She carried her little brother on her back.
senses.exampleCN: 她背着小弟弟。
senses.why: Latin carricare meant to load a cart, and the cart's load became the verb's work.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 carricare 指给车装货，装车的活儿成了这个动词的职责。

senses.title: To support weight
senses.definition: to hold up the weight of a structure or person
senses.definitionCN: 撑住建筑或人的重量
senses.example: The bridge can carry heavy trucks.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥能承载重卡。
senses.why: A loaded cart rests on its wheels; supports too bear the load.
senses.whyCN: 装满的车压在轮上，支撑物同样负重。

senses.title: To take news, disease or sound along
senses.definition: to spread news, disease, electricity or sound from place to place
senses.definitionCN: 把消息、疾病、电流或声音带往各处
senses.example: Mosquitoes can carry malaria.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子会传播疟疾。
senses.why: What a cart carries travels far, and so do news and germs in their own vehicles.
senses.whyCN: 车能载物远行，消息与病菌也各有自己的「车」。

senses.title: To keep on with an action
senses.definition: to put a plan or task into action, as in carry out
senses.definitionCN: 把计划或任务付诸实施，如 carry out
senses.example: They carried out the fire drill calmly.
senses.exampleCN: 他们冷静地完成了消防演习。
senses.why: A plan is like cargo: it must be loaded onto action and delivered.
senses.whyCN: 计划如货物，须装上「行动」并送达。

senses.example: In that case, we will take the earlier bus.

intro.en: Cat is a short, ancient word that walked through many languages.

items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 cattus 指家猫，多认为借自沙漠地区的语言。

items.en: German Katze and Dutch kat are the same word in sibling tongues.
items.cn: 德语 Katze 与荷兰语 kat 是同词的兄弟形式。

items.en: Modern English extended cat to lions, tigers and even jazz musicians.

definition_zh: 抓住；接住；赶上（车）；染上（病）；引起注意
definition_en: to take hold of something moving, to stop and hold it, to board in time, or to get an illness
core_image: 伸出手，在东西飞走的瞬间把它按住
scene: 体育课的自由活动时间，男生们在操场上练习接球。During break the boys practised how to catch a high ball on the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 catch 是「接住」（第 1 个义项：伸手接住移动之物）；句意为课间在操场练接高球。

derivatives.zh: 由 catch 加 -er 构成，义为「接球手；捕手」
由 catch 加 -ing 构成，义为「传染性的；动人的」

senses.title: To take hold of something moving
senses.definition: to stop and hold something that is moving or falling
senses.definitionCN: 截住并握住移动或坠落之物
senses.example: He caught the ball with one hand.
senses.exampleCN: 他单手接住了球。
senses.why: The word grew from chasing: to catch is to reach the thing that tries to leave.
senses.whyCN: 此词由「追逐」生长：接住，就是追上那个想逃的东西。

senses.title: To reach a bus, train or person in time
senses.definition: to arrive in time for a bus, train or meeting
senses.definitionCN: 及时到达以乘上车或见到人
senses.example: We ran to catch the last bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们跑去赶末班车。
senses.why: Chasing does not always mean grabbing; sometimes just boarding in time.
senses.whyCN: 追逐未必动手，有时只是及时登上一班车。

senses.title: To get an illness
senses.definition: to become ill with a disease that spreads
senses.definitionCN: 染上会传染的病
senses.example: She caught a cold in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她在雨里着凉感冒了。
senses.why: A disease moves from person to person like something that leaps and must be seized.
senses.whyCN: 疾病在人间跳来跳去，像非要抓住不可的东西。

senses.title: To draw attention
senses.definition: to attract the eye or interest
senses.definitionCN: 把目光或兴趣吸引过来
senses.example: A red scarf caught my eye.
senses.exampleCN: 一条红围巾吸引了我。
senses.why: The eye too reaches out and seizes what glides past it.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛也会伸手，一把抓住掠过的东西。

senses.title: To trap or entangle
senses.definition: to become stuck or tangled in something
senses.definitionCN: 被某物卡住或缠住
senses.example: His sleeve caught on the door handle.
senses.exampleCN: 他的袖子被门把手钩住了。
senses.why: What is seized may simply be held fast, stuck like a fish in a net.
senses.whyCN: 被抓住的东西只是被扣住，像网中的鱼。

intro.en: Catch began as a hunter's word for chasing down prey.
intro.cn: catch 起初是猎人追捕猎物的用词。

items.en: Old North French cachier meant to chase.
items.cn: 古法语北部方言 cachier 意为追逐。

items.en: It descends from Latin captare, to try to seize, a frequentative of capere.

items.en: Norse ketcha reinforced the English form and its chase sense.
items.cn: 诺斯语 ketcha 强化了英语的词形与追逐义。

items.en: Middle English catch meant to pursue, seize and trap.
items.cn: 中古英语 catch 兼指追、抓与困住。

items.en: Modern catch added buses, colds and attention.
items.cn: 现代 catch 又添赶车、感冒与吸引诸义。

动词，义为「抓取」，动作急促。

entries.definition: To fail to catch or hit.

definition_zh: 原因；起因；事业；导致；引起
definition_en: the reason something happens, a principle people fight for, or to make something happen
core_image: 第一块倒下的多米诺骨牌，推倒了后面一整排
scene: 实验课后，大家一起讨论这次泡沫喷发的原因。After the experiment the class discussed the cause of the foam eruption.
sceneCN: 这里 cause 是「原因」（第 1 个义项：使某事发生的东西）；句意为课后讨论泡沫喷发的原因。

senses.title: The reason something happens
senses.definition: the person, event or thing that makes something happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生的人、事件或事物
senses.example: Heavy rain was the cause of the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 暴雨是洪水的原因。
senses.why: Latin causa meant a reason argued in court, and the courtroom reason became the everyday one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 causa 指庭上争辩的理由，这理由走下法庭便成了日常的「原因」。

senses.title: A principle worth supporting
senses.definition: a principle or aim that people support or fight for
senses.definitionCN: 人们支持或为之奋斗的原则与目标
senses.example: They raised money for an environmental cause.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为环保事业筹款。
senses.why: A reason you argue for in court is also a side you take; the reason became a banner.
senses.whyCN: 庭上所争之由，也是你所站的一边，理由就此变成旗帜。

senses.title: To make something happen
senses.definition: to make something happen, especially something bad
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生，多指坏事
senses.example: The storm caused several road accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨引发多起车祸。
senses.why: What stands behind an event is also what pushes it into being, so the noun grew a verb.
senses.whyCN: 立于事件之后者，也是把它推进存在者，名词于是长出了动词。

senses.title: To mark a happy event with joy
senses.definition: to take part in enjoyable activities for a special day or success
senses.definitionCN: 以欢乐活动纪念特殊日子或成功
senses.example: We celebrate Spring Festival with dumplings.
senses.exampleCN: 我们吃饺子庆祝春节。
senses.why: Latin celebrare meant to visit often and honour in crowds, and honouring turns into partying.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 celebrare 指常去、聚众礼赞，礼赞渐变为欢庆。

senses.title: To praise someone or something
senses.definition: to praise publicly in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 以言语或文字公开赞美
senses.example: The poem celebrates the courage of the firefighters.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗讴歌消防员的勇气。
senses.why: To honour a thing repeatedly is to praise it, so the word kept that face too.
senses.whyCN: 反复礼赞即是称颂，这个词也保留了这一面。

senses.title: To perform a religious rite
senses.definition: to perform a ceremony, especially a religious one

senses.example: The priest celebrated Mass on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 神父周日主持弥撒。
senses.why: Crowd-honouring was first of all a public rite, and rites still need someone to lead.

intro.en: Celebrate goes back to a Latin word for honouring something in a crowd.
intro.cn: celebrate 上溯拉丁语「聚众礼赞」之词。

items.en: Latin celebrare meant to frequent, honour and perform in company.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celebrare 意为常至、礼赞、聚众而行。

items.en: Its root celebris described a place thronged with many people.
items.cn: 词根 celebris 形容「人头攒动」之地。

items.en: Old French celebrer kept the religious ceremony sense.
items.cn: 古法语 celebrer 保留宗教仪式义。

items.en: Middle English celebrate meant to perform rites and honour publicly.
items.cn: 中古英语 celebrate 兼指行礼与公开礼赞。

items.en: Modern English stressed joyful parties, praise and famous names.
items.cn: 现代英语强调欢庆、赞美与「名人」。

note.en: The first group collects same-root words; the second collects joy-and-praise words.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词，第二组收欢庆与赞美类词。

entries.definition: To keep a festival or custom.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「过（节）；遵守」。

normalIntro.en: Remember celebrate through its crowd-honouring root.

normal.en: celebrate comes from celebris, thronged with people.
normal.cn: celebrate 源自 celebris（人潮涌动）。

normal.en: celebrity is a person much celebrated.
normal.cn: celebrity 即被频频礼赞之人。

normal.en: celebration is the party itself.

normal.en: celebrated means famous.

senses.title: A joyful event for a special day
senses.definition: a party or event held to mark something happy
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念喜事而举行的聚会或活动
senses.example: The wedding celebration lasted till midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 婚庆一直持续到午夜。
senses.why: The Latin celebrare meant honouring in company, and a company-honouring became an event.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 celebrare 意为聚众礼赞，聚众之举便成了一场活动。

senses.title: The act of celebrating
senses.definition: the action of marking a happy occasion
senses.definitionCN: 纪念喜事的行为本身
senses.example: The celebration of the win began in the locker room.
senses.exampleCN: 对胜利的庆祝从更衣室就开始了。

intro.en: Celebration is celebrate wearing its Latin action ending.
intro.cn: celebration 就是 celebrate 戴上拉丁动作后缀。

items.en: Latin celebrare meant to honour and perform publicly.
items.cn: 拉丁语 celebrare 意为公开礼赞与举行。

items.en: Late Latin celebratio named the act of honouring.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 celebratio 指礼赞之行。

items.en: Old French celebration passed the act-name onward.
items.cn: 古法语 celebration 把行为之名传了下去。

items.en: Middle English celebration first meant religious rites.
items.cn: 中古英语 celebration 起初指宗教仪式。

items.en: Modern English generalised it to every joyful event.
items.cn: 现代英语将其泛化为一切欢庆活动。

note.en: The first group collects family words; the second collects festive-event words.
